judgments.rationale: 6-mark trig identity/distribution equation, 3-mark tan, and 6-mark volume integral make trigonometry primary; distribution and integration are independently marked secondary methods.
The 2 marks for the inverse and 3 marks for the composition directly assess Function composition and inverses only.
The 6-mark triangle-length calculation is a geometry/measurement method; no separate trigonometric skill is materially marked.
The 6 marks concern correlation selection and a linear-regression prediction; independent-variable/temperature responses are contextual, not a separate statistics skill.
Both parts are antiderivative work, including the initial condition to fix the constant; integration is the only materially assessed method.
The derivative graph supplies the gradient/normal and concavity reasoning; graph reading is not a separate graph-transformation skill here.
Quadratic root/axis structure is primary; the tangent part also permits and materially marks differentiation, while generic graph structure is not independently required.
The 3-mark tangent, 7-mark area integral, and 2-mark triangle area support calculus as primary; triangle area is the material geometry secondary method.
Finding f from f′ with f(0)=1 is entirely integration plus an initial condition; algebraic manipulation is enabling work, not a separate topic.
The logarithm laws enable the equation, but the separately marked identity/interval solution work makes trigonometry primary; logarithms remain secondary.
The 5-mark enclosed-area part uses integration and the 7-mark maximum-distance part uses differentiation; the 3-mark graph transformation is the only secondary method.
Intercept/asymptote work dominates the function classification, while the 2-mark minimum condition materially invokes differentiation.
The segment area is computed from chord/arc/sector geometry; the official marks do not independently assess a trig or radian skill.
Direction changes and total distance from velocity are kinematics, with integration used to accumulate distance; the given sine is not an independently assessed trig method.
All three 2-mark parts determine and evaluate the sinusoidal water-depth model, assessing trigonometric functions; radians are not separately marked.
Part (a) explicitly assesses composition, while the sketch and exactly-two-solutions condition assess graph behavior; both function skills are material.
The maximum-distance question uses motion relationships and the velocity graph; no separately marked integration method is required by the official scheme.
The maximum/rates/inflexion parts assess differentiation and the volume assesses integration; finding the x-intercept materially assesses polynomial roots as a function secondary.
Bearings, sine-rule distances, and closest-point/boat-speed geometry are all materially marked geometry/trigonometry work; kinematics is not separately assessed.
Composition is explicit in part (a), while the exponential limit in part (b) materially uses exponential/logarithmic relationships; quadratic roots are unsupported.
The rectangle-area maximum is an optimization problem whose marked method is differentiation; graph transformations are not independently assessed.
The one-solution condition is established from the quadratic root/discriminant structure; logarithms are the enabling, separately marked secondary step.
Every part uses vector components, line equations, or a perpendicular dot product; roots are merely algebraic solving, not a material function method.
The sine-rule length and triangle-area calculations are geometric measurement; trigonometry is instrumental rather than a separate marked skill.
The sinusoidal/periodic model and maxima spacing are primary trigonometry; constructing/interpreting the line and tooth model supports the two function secondary skills.
The intercept, maximum point, and sketch are marked as polynomial/graph features; no differentiation or logarithm method is independently required.
The distribution table, normalization for k, and conditional probability are all distribution methods; generic probability is redundant.
The 3-mark volume integral makes calculus primary, while solving the 2-mark point condition uses logarithm laws; geometry/radians are not separate methods.
Acceleration/velocity relationships and the 6-mark recovery of velocity plus 4-mark distance work are kinematics and integration; polynomial roots are not independently assessed.
Both the 3-mark antiderivative and 4-mark volume are direct integration applications; geometry/radian language is contextual.
Recovering f from f′ is integration, and the inflexion/concavity parts use derivative behavior; the given x-intercept does not assess polynomial roots.
The antiderivative and area between the stated boundaries are entirely integration; roots are not a distinct marked method.
Finding n and transforming mean/variance under scaling are summary-statistics operations; no distribution method is assessed.
All three parts differentiate and compare first/second derivatives; logarithm notation in the given function is not a separately marked skill.
The 7-mark sinusoidal model plus 8 marks on speed/acceleration make calculus (kinematics and differentiation) primary, with trigonometric identities secondary.
Segment area and the equation for its angle are handled as circle geometry/measurement; no separate radian skill is awarded.
The vertex/sketch are graph methods and the enclosed area is an integral; roots are not an independently assessed method.
Largest perimeter from two sides and area is a geometry/measurement optimization calculation; trig is instrumental, not separately retained.
Periodic maxima determine the spacing, while the sum of x_k is an arithmetic-series method; both are independently assessed.
The transformed linear model and recovery of n,k use exponent/logarithm laws as the dominant method; the regression fit is materially secondary.
The 3-mark volume calculation is the dominant marked method and uses integration; the given sine/exponential form does not receive an independent taxonomy method label.
Determining the Ferris-wheel parameters and solving the repeated height condition are trigonometric-model equations; other labels are contextual.
Initial value, maximum speed, acceleration, direction change, and total distance materially assess kinematics, differentiation, and integration; the cosine in v(t) is given.
Parallel-vector conditions are solved entirely with vector components; quadratic-root language is not assessed.
The single 8-mark area task is an integration application; algebraic and root manipulations are only enabling steps.
The double-angle/identity calculation for cos 4x is the sole marked method; radians are only domain notation.
The marks explicitly cover quadratic roots/vertex form and reflection/translation, so both function skills are independently assessed; vectors are not.
The 3-mark volume and water-accumulation/empty-space parts use integration; sign and extremum conditions use differentiation. Trigonometry and geometry are context, not separately assessed methods.
The 5-mark intercept/asymptote work and 2-mark limit are graph-feature methods; no polynomial-root method is separately assessed.

Rest, acceleration and total distance are kinematics; the marked work differentiates for acceleration and integrates for distance. The exponential form is supplied, not a separately rewarded logarithm method.
The cosine-rule setup and road-length calculation use trigonometric relationships and geometric lengths. The quadratic is an intermediate solve, not a separately assessed roots skill.
The 9 marks on intersections/terms/21st term assess sequences; solving intersections uses trigonometry and the 4-mark shaded-area response requires an integral.
Recovering f from f′ and a point is an antiderivative-and-constant task; the exponential is part of the supplied derivative, not a separate differentiation or logarithm method.
All 7 marks use intercept changes and translations/scaling of a graph; no roots or independent model-fitting method is assessed.
The full 7-mark task is solving a logarithmic equation, so exponents and logarithms is the sole material skill.
The derivative and tangent-parallel parts dominate (9 marks), while finding tanθ and the line uses trigonometry (6 marks). No separate radians skill is required.
Product differentiation and locating horizontal tangents account for all 6 marks; the exponential factor is not a separately assessed logarithm method.
Sketching f″ and using its sign for inflection and concavity assess derivative behavior throughout; the supplied trigonometric expression is not an independently marked trig skill.
Vector-line and angle work makes geometry/trigonometry primary; the 7-mark composition/inverse part and tangent-slope work materially assess Functions and differentiation.
The 3-mark volume is an integration task; the 2-mark x-intercept requires logarithmic solving. Other geometric labels describe setup rather than marked methods.
Cosine-rule lengths and the triangle-area/angle calculation are geometric measurement methods; no separate trig-identity skill is required.
The rate and most-rapid-increase parts require differentiation; evaluating the supplied logistic model is contextual, not a separate exponent skill.
Motion relationships and total distance/displacement require kinematics and integration; polynomial roots and differentiation are not separately rewarded methods here.
Tangent/normal lines make differentiation dominant; the inverse/reflection relation and p^x/log calculations are material secondary Function and logarithm methods.
The 3-mark parameter determination and 4-mark transformation description assess function modelling and graph transformations; vectors and polynomial-root labels are unsupported.

dV/dx, the critical point and its maximum justification account for the substantive marks and directly assess differentiation/optimization; cuboid geometry is setup.

Stationary points, tangency, inflection/rate work and the rotated volume directly mark differentiation and integration; graph and geometry details are setup.
The normal and binomial flight calculations are probability methods; no descriptive-statistics procedure is separately assessed.
Venn counts and the exclusive-or probability all use event/set probability; the diagram is not a geometry method.
Tangent equations and gradients make differentiation primary; the translated asymptote/graph work and triangle area are material Function and geometry secondary methods.
The 5-mark rotated-region volume is integration; finding the intercept supplies a limit and setup, not a separately assessed graph-transformation method.
The sketch is the central 3-mark graph task, while finding a from the point uses logarithms; the other algebra/root labels are unsupported.
Finding f from f′ and the point is an antiderivative problem; ln 4 and the exponential integrand do not create a separately assessed logarithm skill.
The marked work compares displacement, velocity and speeds of particles, so Kinematics is the material skill; no vector or integration method is assessed.
The values, root solve and local minimum are function/graph technology tasks; no polynomial-root theorem or differentiation method is independently credited.
The f″/concavity parts and antiderivative/area reconstruction directly assess differentiation and integration; the logarithm is embedded in the supplied derivative.
The probability table and maximizing E(X) are discrete-distribution methods throughout; differentiation, roots and generic probability labels add no separately assessed method.
Composition is explicitly worth 2 marks and the inverse-function relationship drives the 5-mark continuation; numerical logarithmic solving is not a separate log-law method.
The trigonometric wheel model/period and chord/central-angle work assess trig and geometric measurement; the final rate calculation materially assesses differentiation.
Reading f, evaluating f∘f and sketching g after a vertical transformation explicitly assess composition/inverses and graph transformations.
The derivative and common-tangent conditions determine h and k in all three parts, so differentiation is the sole material skill.
The identity proof and solution of the interval equation account for all 8 marks and use trigonometric identities/equations.
The discriminant/one-intersection condition, factor form, vertex form and sign/increasing interval assess polynomial roots and graph behavior; differentiation is not required.
Differentiation dominates the stationary/concavity work; the graph sketch and ln inequality materially assess graph features and logarithms.

The identity conversion and interval solution are primarily trigonometric; converting to and solving the quadratic supplies the secondary equations skill.
The 6-mark tangent-gradient calculation requires differentiation; the exact x-intercept calculation materially uses logarithms.
The side lengths, cosine information and area calculation are geometric measurement; trigonometry is embedded in that geometric method.
Both 3-mark parts recover antiderivatives/functions, so Integration is the sole material skill; algebra only determines the constant.

Regression-line calculation, prediction and best-fit drawing account for 6 of 7 marks and are correlation/regression work; the reported means support that workflow rather than a separate descriptive classification.
Wheel dimensions and the sinusoidal height model require geometric measurement and trigonometric periodicity; no calculus or kinematics method is independently assessed.
Finding rest, total distance and acceleration explicitly marks kinematics together with integration and differentiation; no polynomial-root method is required.
[2] intersection work is minor; tangent differentiation and [5] enclosed-area integration dominate, with [2] inverse-function area as a genuine secondary method.

The 13 marks assess radian/periodic trigonometry and geometric lengths/heights; rotation is not a kinematics question.
Finding y from dy/dx and an initial value is antiderivative/integration work; the given trigonometric expression is not a separately assessed geometry method.

The 5-mark solution is a trigonometric equation; the separately marked 2-mark rational decomposition is algebraic manipulation.

Derivative sign/turning-point analysis and area under f′ are explicitly assessed, so differentiation and integration are the only material methods.

All 9 marks use geometric-sequence terms, sums, convergence and a threshold; exponent/log labels are not independently evidenced.

The 5-mark bound/parameter calculation is trigonometric, while the separately marked transformation description earns graph-transformations.
The [9] definite-integral work dominates; the expansion/substitution identity separately assesses algebraic manipulation and trigonometric identities.
Asymptotes and the sketch dominate the function classification; the final separately marked rational inequality earns equations/inequalities.
The least-positive-solution task is a trigonometric equation; radians are notation here rather than an independently evidenced skill.
Binomial coefficients are assessed in [2], and the mean-of-terms condition is solved for x in [5]; both listed number/algebra skills earn marks.
The derivative-based monotonicity/concavity work is dominant; quadratic vertex/roots and the graph information are material function methods.

The median/frequency and standard-deviation calculations are summary-statistics work; no separate distribution method is assessed.

Rest, acceleration and total distance are motion quantities; differentiation and integration are the marked calculus methods.
The pyramid/cuboid dimensions, volume and surface area are geometry/measurement; the 5-mark minimum requires differentiation.
Inverse construction/intersection work and graph transformations dominate the function classification; the enclosed area is an integration secondary.
All five marks recover g from g′ using an antiderivative and the point (0,4); differentiation is not the operation assessed.

Inverse/domain/intersection work is primary; the enclosed area is integration and the equal-gradient condition is differentiation, each explicitly marked.
The tree, conditional events, and expected score use elementary probability throughout; no separate distribution model is required.
Trig amplitude/period/value work dominates, while reading the supplied graph to determine a and b is a material model/graph interpretation method.
Composition earns 2 marks; finding both possible k values requires solving the resulting equation, a material Number and algebra secondary.
The frequency table, cumulative-frequency curve, sampling, and box plot are all descriptive-statistics/frequency-data methods; no separate function skill is marked.

The chord, sector/radian timing and sine-rule parts materially assess trigonometry, exact/radian measure and geometry; the turtle formula is given context, not a separate modelling skill.
Expanding gives 40n, which is a multiple of 10; the sole requested and marked general method is proof/reasoning.

Expanding gives 24n, a multiple of 12; the requested general argument is mathematical proof/reasoning.

The log domain requires the quadratic to be positive for every real x, and the discriminant/root condition is the dominant method; logarithmic-domain recognition is a distinct secondary component in the supplied markscheme evidence.

The question compares and interprets exponential/logistic population models; linear regression is explicitly assessed in (a)-(b), and derivatives are explicitly assessed in (f)-(g), so those are distinct secondary methods.

The first 7 marks assess sinusoidal amplitude/period/phase, while the 9-mark car component assesses kinematics and differentiation; no integration or separate graph-transformation method is directly marked.

The logarithm domain condition is solved through positivity of the quadratic and its discriminant/root structure; the official method does not separately require logarithm laws.

Although regression is assessed in the first 4 marks, most later marks interpret the exponential/logistic models and compare their derivatives; model interpretation is primary with regression and differentiation secondary.
The first 7 marks are sinusoidal amplitude/period/phase work; the car part separately marks motion, derivative acceleration and distance integration, with no Functions graph skill required.

The velocity model is used for extrema, direction, distance and return-to-position; differentiation and integration are explicitly marked alongside the kinematics relationships.

Recovering g from g′ and the initial value is direct integration; the cosine and exponential terms are given rather than separately assessed topics.
The discriminant/root conditions dominate the 5-mark parameter part; the sign-of-roots constraints in (b) are a distinct equations/inequalities method.
The distance is minimized by differentiating x² ln x+4; the square-root/log expression is supplied and no standalone graph or logarithm method is marked.

Quadratic roots/sign analysis and graph asymptotes/intercepts are central; finding k from the maximum also uses logarithm/exponent relationships, while differentiation is only optional.
The 2-mark algebraic decomposition supports a 3-mark antiderivative; the assessed topic is integration rather than generic manipulation.

The tangent gradient and angle condition require differentiation; the cosine model and conversion of the tangent angle use a distinct trigonometric relation.

Stationary points, extrema and inflexion use differentiation, but part (e)'s 4 marks require integrating f′ and applying f(−2)=36 to recover f; the recommendation omitted that assessed integration.
